notes.text: David Jiříček has started playing on the power play: on the ice for 41% of the team’s power-play time in 10 games, up from 2% last season.

The forward lines keep changing. Even their four most-used trios over the last 10 games cover only 32% of their forwards’ 5-on-5 time, the 6th-lowest in the league (a typical team: 42%). The lines listed lean on their latest games, but expect new combinations tonight.

Justin Holl has not dressed for the last 5 games. He is one of their more valuable skaters. Jack St. Ivany has taken his spot beside Cole Hutson. That pair has had 55% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 111:20 together.

Rasmus Sandin is on long-term injured reserve (knee surgery) and has missed the last 16 games. He is a top-four defenseman. Timothy Liljegren has taken his spot beside Martin Fehérváry. That pair has had 53% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 121:13 together.
Jakob Chychrun has started killing penalties: on the ice for 26% of the team’s shorthanded time in 20 games, up from 8% last season.

stakes: The Capitals go in sixth in the Metropolitan with 20 points, 2 points behind the Flyers, fifth. A regulation win for the Capitals would pull them level with the Flyers. The Capitals have five games in hand.

story.head: Tuch’s favorite opponent
paras: The Capitals won the teams’ first meeting this season, 5-2 in Washington on Oct 28. The Caps are on a four-game losing streak, while the Flyers have won two in a row. This is a Metropolitan Division matchup, with the Flyers fifth (tied for 20th in the NHL) and the Capitals sixth (25th).

The Flyers’ record (.440) is about what their chances are worth. The Capitals have played better than their record (.500) says: their chances are worth about .568, and their goaltending has held them back.
This season, the Capitals have been outscored 76-67, even though they’ve outscored teams 50-48 at 5-on-5. On special teams, opponents have outscored them 17-12.

The Flyers play slow, tight games (2nd lowest), take away shots from the point (3rd lowest) and get a lot of their shots blocked (29th). The Capitals, by contrast, get their shots through to the net (5th). Philadelphia has scored 2.52 goals a game, the fourth fewest in the league. As for the Capitals, they have a leaky penalty kill (27th). They also get the league’s best looks (1st), so the Capitals have the edge over the Flyers on shot quality. Washington has allowed 3.80 goals a game, the fourth most in the league. The Capitals’ knack for getting shots through meets a team that blocks a lot.

Matvei Michkov (11 G / 8 A / 19 P in 25 GP) leads the Flyers in scoring, and Trevor Zegras (5 G / 10 A / 15 P in 25 GP) is next in line. Alex Tuch (13 G / 3 A / 16 P in 20 GP) is tied for the Capitals’ scoring lead, with a point in eight straight games against Philadelphia. Ryan Leonard (9 G / 7 A / 16 P in 20 GP) shares it.
Joseph Woll (5-6-2 / .892 SV% in 13 GS) will likely start for Philadelphia, and Logan Thompson (7-6-0 / .879 SV% in 15 GS) for Washington.
At home, Spencer Carbery likes to send Protas, Dubois and Tuch out against the other team’s top line, so watch for them against Foerster, Zegras and Konecny.
